title: Germ-free Drosophila melanogaster Colonization with Propionibacterium Biofilms
author: Bronnec, Alexeyev

steps.title: Prepare biological safety cabinet
steps.instruction: Purge the BSC by turning it on at least 5 min before work, disinfect interior with bleach solution or 70 % ethanol, wipe every item to be introduced with 70 % ethanol, wear gloves and disinfect them with 70 % ethanol, arrange work zones as clean/working/dirty, minimize movements and keep the airflow grill unobstructed.

steps.title: Assemble sterile washing kit
steps.instruction: Autoclave empty vials with cotton plugs, wrap tightly in aluminum foil and keep dry; prepare 2.7 % sodium hypochlorite, 70 % ethanol, and sterile milli‑Q water each warmed to ~30 °C; gather sterile petri dish, painting brush (pre‑washed in 70 % ethanol), plastic transfer pipette, blotting paper, and 40 µm cell strainer (all purchased sterile). Sterilize reusable items (brush, blotting paper) in autoclave cycles of 20 min at 121 °C.

steps.title: Transfer fruit flies between vials
steps.instruction: In the BSC, spray‑off all vials (including cotton plug exterior) with 70 % ethanol and let dry. To stun, tap the source vial gently until flies fall to the bottom and remain immobilized for ~2 s; keep tapping to maintain position. As an alternative, place the vial horizontally on ice for a few minutes, rotating periodically, until flies become inactive. Prepare the destination vial nearby, open it, tape down the source vial, quickly remove its cotton plug and invert onto the new plug, then tap the two vials together to move all flies. Place vials sideways to allow recovery. Avoid moist or liquid media that could trap flies.

steps.title: Incubate fruit flies
steps.instruction: Maintain flies at 25 °C with ~60 % humidity (or 18–25 °C out of direct sunlight if no incubator). Keep the food moist; avoid dry conditions. Transfer flies to fresh vials every 2–3 weeks, adjusting frequency based on population density. Typical density is ~50 flies per vial; for experiments use ~30 flies per vial without sex sorting.

steps.title: Euthanize and dispose of flies
steps.instruction: Freeze flies in a vial for ≥24 h or dump stunned flies into a container filled with ethanol or isopropanol. Dispose of the waste as solid, non‑sharps biohazard according to laboratory regulations.

steps.title: Prepare Propionibacterium biofilm
steps.instruction: All work is done anaerobically in jars with an atmosphere‑generation sachet; incubations at 37 °C, 250 rpm for planktonic steps. 1) Plate: scratch frozen Propionibacterium glycerol stock with a sterile loop, streak onto a blood agar plate, invert and incubate anaerobically at 37 °C for 72 h. 2) Preculture: pick one colony, inoculate 10 mL BHI‑glycerol (BHIg) broth, incubate anaerobically at 37 °C, 250 rpm for 48 h. 3) Biofilm culture: add 9.5 mL BHIg to a T‑25 flask, inoculate with 0.5 mL preculture, incubate horizontally at 37 °C for 6 days anaerobically, changing medium every 48 h. For each change, tilt the flask ~45° for ~10 min at 18–25 °C to let the biofilm pellet at the corner, carefully pipette off ~8 mL supernatant, discard, and slowly add 10 mL fresh BHIg.

substeps.instruction: Plate frozen glycerol stock on blood agar; incubate 37 °C, 72 h anaerobically.
Pick a colony into 10 mL BHIg; incubate 37 °C, 250 rpm, 48 h anaerobically.
Inoculate 9.5 mL BHIg in T‑25 flask with 0.5 mL preculture; incubate horizontally 37 °C, 6 days anaerobically.
Every 48 h, tilt flask ~45° for ~10 min (18–25 °C), let biofilm settle, remove ~8 mL supernatant, add 10 mL fresh BHIg.
